subject: Post-call: ACME evaluation — latency & throughput A/B plan
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T14:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: ACME evaluation — latency & throughput A/B plan

Hi Sam / ACME evals team,

Great to speak earlier — thanks for walking us through the production constraints and the 1.5M daily inference budget. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of pain:
- p95 tail from current vendor rises substantially under bursty traffic (seen ~350–420ms).
- Token throughput requirement: sustained ~45k tokens/sec for embedding pipeline, spikes to ~120k tokens/sec for batch summarization.
- Need comparatives vs HyperscalerX and CloudVendor (the team you mentioned).

What Redwood will deliver for the next test sprint (proposed):
1) Two A/B lanes: Redwood-hosted (production config) vs HyperscalerX-managed endpoint.
2) Bench plan focused on p95 / p99 and tokens/sec under three load patterns: steady, burst, and cold-start heavy KV-cache miss.
3) Collect token-level traces and cost-per-1k-token estimate for each lane.
4) Short report + CSV export with raw times for your ingest.

Attachments: throughput-test-plan.md (short test script + traffic profiles), acme-hyperscaler-comparison.csv (sample schema) — I included placeholders you can open.

Proposed timeline:
- Monday (12/07): Redwood runs baseline tests on your sample dataset (we need a 1GB anonymized sample log).
- Wednesday (12/09): A/B experiments completed; Thursday (12/10) recap call.

Questions for you:
- Can you share a 1GB anonymized sample or point us to a shared S3 with read access?
- Any hard p95 SLO you must meet (e.g., p95 < 250ms)?

Next steps: Sam, if that timeline works, I’ll schedule the internal run this Monday and loop Ben from CloudVendor for parity runs.

Thanks —
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
attachments: throughput-test-plan.md (text/markdown), acme-hyperscaler-comparison.csv (text/csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Sam Park <sam@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T16:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME evaluation — latency & throughput A/B plan

Diego — good notes. Two quick product clarifications to feed into the plan: 

1) Test variants: please include (a) Redwood default quantized profile, (b) Redwood dense FP16 profile, and (c) HyperscalerX default. That helps us show cost vs quality.
2) KV cache cold-start: add a 0→50 concurrent session ramp to simulate cache misses — we’ve seen p99 blow up in that window.

Also: I’ll run a short internal eval to capture model-serving kernel choices (CUDA kernels) that can explain a ~10–20% gap. Sean has the bench infra; Sean, can you reserve the 4xA100 slot Monday morning?

—Marissa
Product Lead, Performance
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Park <sam@acme.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Cho <ben@cloudvendor.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME evaluation — latency & throughput A/B plan

Thanks Diego / Marissa — that timeline looks good. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can share a 1GB anonymized sample S3 link by EOD today (I’ll send credentials).
- Our target SLO is p95<=240ms for user-facing prompt completions; for batch summarization p95<=600ms is acceptable.
- Can you also capture tokens/sec measured as "tokens generated / sec" and "tokens processed / sec" separately? We have different billing buckets.

One more ask: Ben from CloudVendor said he can run the same script from their managed endpoint on 12/08 to match your Wednesday run — Ben, are you ok with that?

Sam
Lead ML Engineer, ACME.ai

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Park <sam@acme.ai>, Ben Cho <ben@cloudvendor.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-07T07:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME evaluation — latency & throughput A/B plan

Sam — thanks for the quick reply and the S3 share (I have the link). Confirming the plan with measurable outputs: 

Bench plan highlights (attached: throughput-test-plan.md):
- Metrics captured: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec (generated / processed), tail percentiles during cold-starts, cost-per-1k-tokens estimate.
- Load patterns: steady 50k tokens/sec for 15m, burst 0→120k tokens/sec over 60s repeated 6x, cold-start ramp (50 new sessions in 120s).
- Model variants: Redwood-FP16, Redwood-Quant, HyperscalerX-default, CloudVendor-default.
- Data collection: CSV rows with timestamp, route, model_variant, tokens_generated, tokens_processed, latency_ms_p95, latency_ms_p99, cost_estimate_usd_per_1k_tokens.

Preliminary baseline numbers (local dev run, not final) — included as a quick sanity check:
- Redwood-FP16 (steady): p95=180ms, p99=240ms, tokens_processed=48k/s
- Redwood-Quant (steady): p95=220ms, p99=300ms, tokens_processed=60k/s (higher TPS but slightly worse tail)
- HyperscalerX-default (steady): p95=265ms, p99=380ms, tokens_processed=50k/s

Notes: Redwood-Quant improves throughput by enabling denser packing of activations but increases tail for cold-starts; include warm-up runs in your script.

Ben — can you confirm you’ll run the identical script on 12/08 and share raw CSVs? If you prefer, we can spin up a short shared GCS bucket to drop results.

Next steps / calendar:
- Mon 12/07: Redwood runs internal baseline (done).
- Tue 12/08: HyperscalerX parity run (Ben + ACME) / Redwood final A/B runs.
- Thu 12/10: Recap call (30m) to review p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost tradeoffs.

I attached the throughput-test-plan.md and a small example CSV to show the output schema.

Cheers,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
attachments: acme-hyperscaler-comparison.csv, throughput-test-plan.md, acme-logs-sample.zip

From: Sam Park <sam@acme.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Cho <ben@cloudvendor.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME evaluation — latency & throughput A/B plan

Confirmed — thanks everyone. Ben has the script and will drop results to the shared bucket by EOD. We’ll validate p95 <= 240ms for prompt completions; if Redwood’s FP16 baseline holds at ~180ms p95 as shown we’ll move to an on-site pilot next quarter.

I’ll see you on Thu 12/10 for the recap.

Best,
Sam
Lead ML Engineer, ACME.ai
